Find your reset time

Codex Usage Limits: Check Your Allowance and Reset Time

If you sign in to Codex with ChatGPT, open the Codex usage dashboard and check the reset time next to the allowance you used up. In Codex CLI, start with /status. If you use your own API key, check the API project’s limits and billing instead.

  1. Find which limit you reached
  2. Read 5-hour, weekly or monthly limits
  3. Check API rate limits and billing
  4. Check an unclear limit or reset
  5. CLI test and sources

Which limit did you reach?

See stepsSee stepsSee steps

Read your 5-hour, weekly or monthly Codex limit

  1. Open the Codex usage dashboard. In ChatGPT Desktop, check Settings → Usage & billing where available. Make sure the workspace matches the one where the task stopped.
  2. Read the allowance label, its remaining amount and the reset time alongside it. Plans can show different windows. In plans with both 5-hour and weekly allowances, the same work can count toward both and they can refresh at different times.
  3. Use the options on that account’s limit notice. If both applicable windows are exhausted, check both after the earlier reset. The other window may still block the same task. A monthly allowance or workspace budget can have a different reset schedule.

For example, if the 5-hour allowance has refreshed and the applicable weekly allowance still shows 0% remaining, check the weekly reset time or the options offered on the notice. Use the displayed time and time zone when deciding when to retry.

There is no universal fixed number of tasks per window. The selected model, context and work performed affect consumption. Tasks in other supported products may also draw from a shared allowance depending on your plan. The current pricing documentation lists the plan-specific rules.

Scheduled refresh, reset and credits

A scheduled refresh follows the allowance’s displayed period. If your account offers a one-time banked reset, check which allowances it covers before redeeming it. Some accounts also show a paid reset or extra credits. Review the exact scope and price before choosing an option, then return to Usage to verify the new balance and time. A subscription billing date can differ from the usage refresh date.

In a managed workspace, ask your administrator about the effective user limit, shared budget and any applicable reset period. Access to the workspace’s usage and credit details can depend on its billing setup.

Check API rate limits and billing

If Codex uses your API key, check the selected API organization and project. Open the API limits page and compare the error with the model’s request or token rate limit. A transient rate limit can clear as capacity becomes available. If the error concerns quota or billing, check the project’s API usage and the organization’s billing status.

The API rate-limit guide explains response headers and retry behavior. Read the full error before retrying. A ChatGPT subscription refresh does not change an API project’s rate limit.

Check an unclear notice or a reset that passed

  • In an active CLI session, run /status for session configuration and usage. Use codex login status in your terminal to check the recorded sign-in method. If you use a custom provider or workspace configuration, confirm the provider shown by your client too.
  • For a context-window or token-count issue, check the session itself. The local Codex token reader explains what JSONL counters represent. Those counters cannot reveal the remaining subscription allowance or an API bill.
  • If the reset time passed and access has not returned, reopen Usage, check the correct workspace and look for a second exhausted allowance or a model-specific notice. If it still looks wrong, contact OpenAI Support with the redacted notice, client, model and time zone.

What the CLI check showed

On November 28, 2026, we ran a read-only account rate-limit request through Codex CLI 0.164.0 using an existing ChatGPT sign-in. It returned a primary window of 10,080 minutes (one week), a reset timestamp and no secondary window in that snapshot. The response did not establish which allowances other accounts see. Download the redacted result summary.

OpenAI documents the App Server protocol and the CLI usage commands. For account-level decisions, see Using Codex with your plan and How Codex resets work. Sources checked November 28, 2026.
